rows.description: My younger sibling follows me everywhere and copies me, and I am annoyed and secretly flattered. Wise: give some time and boundaries, remembering I am their model. Harmful: mocking their need.

rows.description: An elder sibling paid for my coaching or covered for me, and I feel thankful yet pressured. Wise: thank them in words and actions and do not let debt become silence. Harmful: pretending it was nothing.

rows.description: My sibling is jealous of my grades or friends and needles me. Wise: stay kind, share what I can, and avoid boasting. Harmful: pushing back with put-downs.

rows.description: I told my best friend something private and it spread. I feel sick and exposed. It is not my fault for trusting. Wise: confront calmly, reassess what to share with them, and tell a trusted adult if it hurts badly.

rows.description: I leaked a friend's secret out of excitement and now I cannot face them. Wise: apologise plainly with no excuse, accept their anger, and give distance. Harmful: denying it or blaming them.

rows.description: I imagine exposing their secrets in return. Wise: feel the rage, tell it to someone safe, and choose not to do it since revenge makes me the second betrayer. Harmful: acting on it.

rows.description: They deny leaking and say I am overreacting or imagining it. Wise: trust my own memory, keep details, and step back. This is not my fault. Harmful: doubting myself until I apologise.
